meta.title: Accessibility and keyboard
meta.description: The keyboard map, the roles and names the component gives its parts, and what it announces — in one place.

basics.intro: Every capability page has an accessibility section of its own; this page is the summary. The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA, checked by axe in three engines on every change, and by hand with NVDA and VoiceOver before a release.

keyboard.intro: The keys the component uses. Everything else is the browser’s.
rows: Moves to the next control of the schedule, in reading order.
Activates the focused card, chip or button.
Closes the topmost dialog and returns focus to whatever opened it.
keyboard.order: The tab order is the reading order: the pinned chips, the top navigation, then the shifts in order with their cards and their More chips, then the bottom navigation, then the button back to the top. Focus is always visible — a two-pixel ring, offset by two.

points: The root is a region, named by aria-label or by your own header through aria-labelledby.
Each shift is a section labelled by its heading, and the heading level starts at headingLevel.
The cards of a shift are a list, so a screen reader announces how many there are.
A card is a button whose name is the item’s title and whose description carries the level and the time, plus any tags.
The pinned strip is a region with a list of chips, and a separate polite live region announces the count when it changes, at most once a second.
The now marker is a separator named after the time it marks.
Color is never the only carrier: a level shows as a color and as a label.
The default preset meets the contrast ratios of WCAG 2.2 AA; the classic preset reproduces the colors it is named after and documents where it falls short.
A disabled item is marked aria-disabled rather than removed from the tab order, so it can still be read.
Dialogs are native <dialog> elements: the browser contains focus and Escape closes them.
aria-label or a header slot names the region; headingLevel fits it into your page’s outline.
Every string and every announcement comes from localization — see Localization.
A card replaced through renderItem has to spread getItemProps, which is what carries the role, the name and the keyboard handling.
There is no roving focus or arrow-key navigation between cards yet; <kbd>Tab</kbd> is the only movement. It is on the <link to="/discover-more/roadmap/">roadmap</link>.
There are no keyboard shortcuts for the navigation buttons.
The classic preset has known contrast shortfalls, listed under <link to="/discover-more/accessibility/">Accessibility</link>.
